title: NavMesh implementations finding bad paths due to faulty neighbour node updates
body: ### Tested versions Found while using 4.6.stable, has existed for some time, relevant code has been moved around / refactored so didn't dig too far back. ### System information Linux, Godot V4.6.stable + master ### Issue description Hi. I was making a demo app for a devlog to demonstrate why a nav mesh was not going to be suitable for my project, and after bolting on a 2D visibility graph and adding a few procedurally generated 'maps' and code to visualise things, I noticed some rather odd detours being taken in nav-mesh paths. While this was kind of great for my purposes, it felt a little OTT; there seemed to be clearly better corridors it should have taken, using polygons that would surely have been expanded. I was looking at something like the following, but I'm not going to remove the things I've since added, so spoiler alert ;P The orange path is the current implementation (the green is drawn over the top of yellow and orange at start and end). I believe the error is in updating previously visited nodes, specifically this line: modules/navigation_2d/2d/nav_mesh_queries_2d.cpp:299 `if (new_traveled_distance < neighbor_poly.traveled_distance) {` While this is perfectly normal looking for an A* implementation, it is making one very important assumption: that the heuristic does not change. In this not really A* we are doing that does not hold, with the poly position shifting depending on where we are coming from. The update condition needs to be made consistent with the priority queue. ``` float new_distance_to_destination = new_entry.distance_to(p_end_point) * connection_owner->get_travel_cost(); float new_total_travel_cost = new_traveled_distance + new_distance_to_destination; bool update = new_total_travel_cost < neighbor_poly.total_travel_cost() && !Math::is_equal_approx(new_total_travel_cost, neighbor_poly.total_travel_cost()); if (update) { ... } ``` The 'tight' check with the !is_equal_approx() is required to avoid nodes constantly re-opening each other (inf loop), not common but if the geometry & start/end positions are just so... it happens; another consequence of the not really A* we are doing and the fact we have no concept of closed nodes here, and must always re-evaluate and potentially re-open previously visited nodes. How exactly the existing version checking only the travel_cost was avoiding this remains a mystery to me. Some more examples: These are mostly ones that are flattering to the fix of course. They often all find the same path (far less often on bigger meshes though), but that is a boring case to show; and the 'fixed' version sometimes finds a worse path, particularly on very small meshes (one included above, if I uploaded what I intended), but usually better or the same. To get a better/bigger picture, I collected stats from 10000 random pathing runs per map (and three seeds each for the procedural maps), I counted the number of times each achieved a 1st place (shortest path), 2nd, or 3rd (including ties for 1st and 2nd), and reported the percentage of times it achieved that 'rank', and then also the sum of all path distances and a percentage longer than optimal that is. The percentages of 1st and 3rd rankings are probably most interesting, and show the the fixed version generally performs better on all but the tiny toy map. Map1 is a tiny toy map, made in editor. Map2 is procedurally generated, 'buildings' roughly on a grid, fairly small Map3 extends Map2, offsets buildings from the grid a bit more and is much bigger Map4 is procedurally generated, maze-like, but not overly complicated, smallish Map5 is Map4 but bigger Map6 is large (area, not so much verts), editor made, intended to be an RTS like map ``` Run: Map1 (Seed:-1), 10000 paths Rank Percentages Graph/Alg/Var 1st 2nd 3rd Total distances =============================================================== Visibility Graph : 100% 0.0% 0.0% 13860058.183 NavMesh - Base : 84.8% 9.8% 5.4% 13979362.415 (+0.86%) NavMesh - Fixed? More testing with different maps/map-types would obviously be nice, but I've spent too long down this rabbit hole already and will be attending to other things for a while :-) I will get the demo project on github in the next day or two, it is obviously using a modified engine that can run the old code and the proposed fix at the same time. I will get a write up on what I did there and then drop an update here when both are done. ### Steps to reproduce Path on a (reasonably sized) mesh, observe odd detours from the ideal path. Modify code with proposed fix and try again :-) ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Hard to gauge what exactly is required for a minimal setup, but will be uploading demo soon (which is far from minimal, but is mostly visualisation and mesh generation code + a visibility graph in an extension)
